title: Headwear: Bonnet, 1-Front
description: Back view of a handmade bonnet. Bonnet material is bleached white cotton and muslin (now discolored) with small, four-holed shell buttons that attach the caul to the brim. Buttons are engraved with a flower petal design around the button holes. Both the caul and brim are edged with a ruffle. Pintucks decorate the caul. Bonnett could be secured to the head of the wearer with the ties. By the turn of the century (years surrounding 1900 CE), bonnets were popular, especially for older women or married women who preferred to cover their hair which conformed to  style throughout the nineteenth century. This bonnet belonged to Helen Mauck Ball (1886-1984). Helen was the wife of Dr. Clay Adra Ball, MD (1877-1980) who was a Ball descendent of "The Old and Original Muncie Ball Family" of doctors and lawyers. This line of Ball surnames was original to Muncie and not related to the Ball Brothers who founded the Ball Corporation. The Ball Brother moved to Muncie, Indiana from Buffalo, New York.

title: Dress: Lace Evening Gown, 1-Front
description: Front view of a brown lace and velvet evening gown. Gown is backless and closes on the left side with snaps. Front of dress has a shallow v-neckline that plunges down the back in a deep v-shape. Dress back inclues a wide velevet panel extending from the waistline to the hemline.Dress bodice is fitted and the skirt flares out slight at the hemline. A slip would have been worn underneath the dress.This dress was worn by Mrs. W. W. Huntley, the grandmother of Mrs. Frances Petty Sargent. Frances (Bramble) Petty Sargent (1940-2017). After marrying Edmund F. Petty (1928-1985) in 1967, Frances became a well-known philanthropist, volunteer, and beloved community member in Muncie, Indiana and at Ball State University.

description: Side view of a pair of brown leather dress shoes with louis heels. Shoes have a slightly pointed toe, and the vamps are decorated with cutwork designs oulined by beads and sequins. This pair of shoes is part of a collection of shoes that belonged to Elisabeth Woodowrth Ball (1897-1982). Elisabeth was the daughter of George Alexander Ball (1862-1955) and Frances Woodworth Ball (1872-1958). George was one of the five Ball brothers who established the Ball Corporation in Muncie, Indiana. Elisabeth grew up in the Oakhurst house located in Muncie, Indiana on the ground of the Minnetrista Museum & Gardens.

title: Dress: Cotton Chemise Undergarment, 1-Front
description: Front view of an ankle length combination chemise and petticoat. This chemise undergarment dress is also referred to as a corset cover. The undergarment is made from a finely woven white cotton batiste. Bodice, neckline, and hem are decorated with lace insertion. Closure is a row of two-hole buttons down the back center. A  drawstring with tassels is woven through the neckline making it adjustable. This undergarment belonged to Lucina “Lucy” Ball Owsley (1896–1990) was a prominent Muncie native, philanthropist, and the eldest daughter of Frank Clayton Ball (1858-1943) , one of the five founding Ball Brothers of the Ball Corporation, and his wife Elizabeth Brady Ball (née Elizabeth Wolfe Brady, 1867-1944).

title: Headwear: Slouch Hat, 1-Side
description: Side view of a multicolored slouch hat. Hat has a slouching crown surrounded by a wide brim. Base material of the crown and brim is a earthy beige velour embellished with velvet, velour, and other fabric flowers and leaves in greens, blues, and a soft charcoal gray. This hat is from a collection of hats that belonged to Elisabeth Woodowrth Ball (1897-1982). Elisabeth was the daughter of George Alexander Ball (1862-1955) and Frances Woodworth Ball (1872-1958). George was one of the five Ball brothers who established the Ball Corporation in Muncie, Indiana. Elisabeth grew up at Oakhurst house, which now part of Minnestria Museum & Gardens in Muncie, Indiana. She attended Vassar College in Kentucky, where she studied botany. Before the mid 20th century, both women and men commanly wore hats as part of their everyday outfits. Elisabeth’s hat collection ranges from casual garden hats to elegant evening hats, even one featuring a rare ostrich plume (not pictured on the website).

description: Front view of a calf length navy blue wool duster coat with a convertible gray-beige mink collar. Coat is single-breasted and closes at front center with metal shank buttons. This coat and other coats were part of acollection styled by the Rothmoor brand exclusively for the Ball Stores in the 1970s. This coat was originally purchased and worn by Betty J. Elisabeth’s hat collection ranges from casual garden hats to elegant evening hats, even one featuring a rare ostrich plume (not pictured on the website).

title: Dress: Fit-and-Flare Evening Gown, 1-Front
description: Front of white white taffeta dress was worn by Frances Petty Sargent when she was crowned Queen of the Snow Ball in her hometown of Richmond, Virginia in 1954. Petty, son of Margaret Ball Petty, and was involved in many philanthropic efforts, including donating to the David Owsley Museum of Art and the Beeman Historic Costume Collection at Ball State University.
